Activity 3: Swipe Scenarios

How Online Behaviour Adapts and Changes

Unit 2 Launch activity

Quick Start

Time

20–30 minutes

You need

Exercise book, a pen, and the Swipe Scenarios activity.

Hand in

Your exercise book tasks + reflection answers.

Step 1

Understand the Swipes

Each card has a scenario (the situation) and an action (what someone did). Read both sides, then swipe based on your judgement.

← Good & Use Your Name

No need to hide who you are.

→ Good but Stay Anonymous

Better to use a nickname.

↑ It Depends…

This one is complicated.

↓ Not OK Online

This shouldn't happen.

Step 2

Play Swipe Scenarios

Your goal is to sort the cards by swiping them to the best category.

  • Read the scenario and action carefully.
  • Swipe in the direction that matches your judgement.
  • If you're unsure, use It Depends… and explain why later.
Launch activity
Step 3

Exercise Book Tasks

After completing the game, write answers for the prompts below:

  • From "Not OK Online": Choose one card and explain why this behaviour is never acceptable.
  • From "Good & Use Your Name": Choose one card and explain why being yourself is good in this situation.
  • From "Good but Stay Anonymous": Choose one card and explain why staying anonymous makes sense.
  • From "It Depends…": Choose 3–4 cards and explore what makes each one complicated.
Step 4

Reflection

A. Adapting Your Behaviour

Think about your sorted cards. Why do people behave differently on different platforms?

B. Context Collapse

What happens when something you post for your friends is suddenly seen by teachers, parents, or strangers? How does this change things?

By the end of this task, you should be able to…

  • Identify ways online behaviour changes across different platforms
  • Explain how digital identity can evolve over time
  • Recognise when behaviour needs to adapt for safety, privacy, or wellbeing
  • Understand the concept of "context collapse" in online spaces
